chapter.publish_chronicler_prompt: This chapter has been published. Delegate the internal Chronicler to organize this chapter: read the current chapter text and related records, extract explicit hard facts, character state changes, character/entity relationship changes, location/item/faction changes, and continuity state, then save them with the available tools. Do not rewrite the chapter text.
chapter.write_this_hint: Runs outline → brief → draft → review for this chapter
chapter.settle_this_prompt:
Settle this chapter: {label}.
Read only this chapter's text and extract character state changes, new foreshadowings, paid-off foreshadowings, setting additions and unresolved threads. List additions/changes first, then call the tools to write them into character profiles, foreshadowings, lore entries and story snapshots. Do not modify the text and do not create duplicates; list any item you could not save and why.
chapter.write_need_outline: This chapter has no outline yet
chapter.write_need_outline_body: Add a chapter outline first (goal, characters, conflict, closing hook) so the draft can stay consistent with the story bible and the previous chapter. Add it now?
chapter.settle_list_prompt:
Produce a settle list for this chapter: {label}.
Read only this chapter's body; list additions/changes in five categories: character state changes / newly planted foreshadowings / paid-off foreshadowings / lore additions / unresolved clues.
One item per line, in exactly this format: - category | subject | what to write.
This turn only list the items; do not call any write tool, do not modify character profiles, foreshadowings or lore. Finish with one line stating how many items there are and telling the author to press Confirm import.
chapter.review_hint: Issue list only (typos, names, timeline, unpaid foreshadowings, AI flavor). Does not touch the body.
chapter.review_prompt:
Review this chapter: {label}.
Read the body only and list issues in five categories: 1) typos/grammar (quote the sentence) 2) inconsistent names, titles or identities (quote both conflicting lines) 3) timeline or location conflicts 4) foreshadowings that should have been paid off 5) AI-flavored clichés (quote and suggest a replacement).
One item per line: - category | quoted line or location | problem | suggested fix.
Do not edit the body and do not call write tools this turn; if there are no issues, say so plainly instead of inventing filler.
chapter.settle_apply_hint: Write exactly the items in the settle list above; anything not listed stays untouched
chapter.settle_apply_prompt:
Import the settle list from the previous message: {label}.
Write only the items already listed; leave everything else untouched, and explain separately any item that could not be written. Finish with one line reporting what was actually written.
chapter.settle_this_hint: Write character states, foreshadowings and threads back into the story bible
chapter.outline_draft_hint: Generate this chapter's outline in five fields: goal / cast / conflict / turn / hook
chapter.brief_draft_hint: List 3-5 scenes first (when/where, POV, what advances, conflict, hook), then write the body
chapter.brief_draft_prompt:
Produce the pre-write briefing for this chapter: {label} (chapter id: {id}).
Do only this — do not write the body yet. List 3-5 scenes in this format:
Scene N | when & where | POV | what it advances | conflict or obstacle | hook at the end.
Every scene must trace back to the chapter outline and character profiles. When done, use the Write tool to save this scene list into chapters/{id}/brief and leave the body untouched. Reply in chat with one line only: "Briefing ready — press Write this chapter when you confirm".
chapter.write_prev_unsettled: The previous chapter is not settled yet
chapter.write_prev_unsettled_body: "{label}" has text but has not been settled. Writing the next chapter without settling means character states and new foreshadowings never reach the story bible, and this chapter will not connect.
chapter.write_overwrite_title: This chapter already has body text
chapter.write_overwrite_body: "{label}" already has body text. The AI will produce a candidate draft. Your current text is not overwritten immediately: the write goes into pending changes first, and you decide in the editor whether to keep or discard it. Generate now?
